Elena — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together the quick matrix and proposed terms; see summary below and attached worksheet. I'll also upload the detailed per-model throughput assumptions to the Drive link. High-level answers: 1) Minimum footprint: operationally we recommend 20 min GPUs for a 20 qps steady-state with conservative batching (gpt-opt-6B equivalent). That gives ~60% headroom for diurnal spikes and keeps tail latency under 300ms p95. 2) Decommit windows: our standard is a 30-day notice with a 2-week staged rampdown. For deal flexibility we can offer a 45-day ramp with a 30% partial-credit if you downscale after the first 90 days (this is the grace economics for early adjustments). 3) Warm-start recommendation: enable a 2-week warm-start with incremental 50% burst capacity available from our shared pool; we parameterize this as \"burst lane\" and it costs a smaller, timebound fee.

Proposed ramp schedule (week cadence):
- Week 0-2: Warm-start, 40 GPUs provisioned (20 dedicated, 20 burst) to preload KV caches and pre-warm commonly used models.
- Week 3-6: Steady activation, target consumption moves to 20-25 dedicated GPUs as traffic normalizes.
- Month 2-3: Optimize: we run a batching/caching pass (Redwood Optimize) — expected effective reduction of token cost by 18-25% and can consider a formal downscale if utilization < 55% over a rolling 14d period.

Fallbacks and reliability guardrails: if dedicated capacity is saturated we route non-SLA traffic to a pinned open-model hosted lane (same model family, quantized) to preserve latency-sensitive flows. We also recommend an SLO window for big-batch jobs to be queued during off-peak.

I've attached acromed-dedicated-offer-v2.xlsx and a cluster-sizing-worksheet.csv. High-level numbers are in the worksheet; we can tailor by model mix in the Drive doc.

Elena — quick technical note to complement Priyom's commercial summary. Two items from our infra team: 1) Minimum GPUs: 20 dedicated GPUs is achievable but we'll ask you to pin model families (e.g., mixture of gpt-opt-6B for embeddings and redwood-tuned-3B for generation) so the kernel selection and sequence-length distribution are deterministic. Without pinning, throughput swings require a 1.2x top-up on average. 2) Decommit mechanics: staged rampdown is handled at the infra orchestration layer — step 1 disables new slot allocation, step 2 drains KV cache over 48–72 hours per pod, step 3 reclaims devices. Because GPU provisioning has a warm/cold state, we surface a 72-hour cold-restart SLA for capacity to return to a prior committed size. If you need more aggressive re-provisioning, we can provide reserved warm spares but that's an additional monthly carry fee.

Operational checklist we suggest adding to the contract as exhibits: model pin list, warm-spare option, burst-lane throttles, and a utilization-triggered optimization clause with explicit thresholds. Happy to iterate on wording.
